snippet.title: The Town That Couldn't Wake Up 😯
snippet.description:
What if every time you fell asleep - there was a chance you wouldn’t wake up? 

In 2013 people in Kalachi, Kazakhstan, began falling into sudden comas. 
Kids walking to school dropped mid step and taxi drivers blacked out behind the wheel. 

When the villagers finally woke up days later… they couldn’t remember anything.

Doctors rushed in and ran every test they could think of.
But everything came back clean, and people grew convinced the land itself was cursed.

The comas kept spreading and over 160 people collapsed. 
So the government evacuated the entire village and left Kalachi a ghost town overnight.

Years later, the terrifying truth was discovered: the abandoned uranium mines beneath the town were leaking toxic gas. Silently suffocating the whole village as they slept.

snippet.title: How a Deaf Man Changed Music Forever 🎹🎵
snippet.description:
How did Beethoven compose music if he was deaf?

In the 1790s, Beethoven’s reputation as a musical prodigy was exploding across Europe.

He moved to Vienna in 1792 to compete at the highest level of music.
But then, disaster struck: just as his career was taking off, Beethoven began losing his hearing.

He tried everything to cure it, but when nothing worked he fell into deep depression and feared his life as a musician was over.

But then in a stroke of genius: Beethoven adapted.

He attached a metal rod to his piano and bit down on it as he played.

The vibrations from the piano traveled through his jaw and skull, reaching his inner ear through bone conduction.

So instead of hearing the music, Beethoven found a way to feel it.

Addiction is a condition where a person feels a constant need for a particular substance or activity despite negative consequences. snippet.title: Crash Course Scientific Thinking Preview
snippet.description:
Science is one of the best ways we have of understanding what’s going on around us. In Crash Course Scientific Thinking we’ll explore the foundational principles that underlie scientific thought. 

Course Description
In 7 episodes, Crash Course Scientific Thinking will teach learners the foundational principles underlying scientific thought, pulling back the curtain on processes like peer review, interrogating what makes sources reliable (or not), unpacking how consensus is reached, and revealing how scientific understanding changes over time. Ultimately, learners will gain the ability to think more critically about the scientific information they encounter in their everyday lives. 

Series Objectives
- Describe the dynamic, communal nature of science, articulating the roles of uncertainty and consensus.
- Explain the role of peer review and replication in science.
- Unpack the potential for bias and error in science and understand its self-correction mechanisms.
- Understand the role of specialization in scientific expertise.
- Interpret primary, secondary, and tertiary sources, and use lateral reading to verify claims.
- Understand basic statistical language used to describe scientific findings.

Sources: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Kv2_mFsDxQURuFDxpflD45dy-pCxlqnM9iPSNYxigmQ/edit?tab=t.0#heading=h.vk5i2fgqyumq

Welcome to Crash Course Geology! Over the course of 25 episodes, Sage will introduce you to the incredible geological forces, cycles, and processes that shape our world. This series will explore how geology touches all of our lives — and connects us to a much bigger story.

Course Description
In 25 episodes, we’re going to learn about geology—the study of Earth’s physical structure and processes. Our host, Sage, will teach you about the geological forces and cycles that shape our planet’s past, present, and future. 

This content is based on an introductory university-level curriculum. By the end of this course, you should be able to: 

Trace Earth’s development from its earliest periods to its current structure
Understand the forces of plate tectonics and how they shape Earth’s landscape
Describe the formation of geologic elements like minerals, rocks, and gems 
Identify geologic forces and cycles that impact the earth, while dispelling myths about extreme geological hazards
Learn what geology reveals about Earth’s distant past and what it can teach us about our current changing climate
Explore the geology of other planets within the context of Earth’s unique and common qualities and phenomena
Become familiar with different specialities within geology and what different types of geologists do

Key texts cited include:
Marshak, Stephen. 2021. Earth: Portrait of a Planet, Seventh Edition.
Babcock, Loren E. 2009. Gemstones and Precious Metals.

snippet.title: The Lions That Refused To Eat Her 🦁🧒
snippet.description:
Police in Ethiopia found a missing girl who was guarded by three massive lions... but the reason why they didn't eat her will blow your mind.

In 2005, this 12 year old girl had been missing for over a week.
Seven men had dragged her into the wilderness and planned to force her into a marriage she didn’t want.

The situation was hopeless for the girl but then her kidnappers made one fatal mistake.

While moving camp, the kidnappers walked straight into the territory of three massive lions.

As the lions approached the men they panicked and ran for their lives. 
So they ended up leaving the girl behind to be eaten.

But then the strangest thing happened.

Instead of attacking, the lions walked up to the girl… and quietly sat around her.
They formed a protective circle and looked after her - as if she were one of their own cubs.

Police finally arrived expecting a tragedy but the moment the lions saw the officers, they simply stood up… and walked away - because experts later realized the truth…

The girl had been crying in fear, and her soft whimpers sounded exactly like a distressed cub.
So the lions never saw her as prey - just a baby that needed protection.

snippet.title: California's Most Mysterious Lake Has a Massive Catch
snippet.description:
California's Salton Sea is ground zero for a revolutionary clean energy boom, where eleven active geothermal plants are now using Direct Lithium Extraction to pump battery-grade "white gold" straight from boiling underground brine. By pulling lithium directly from the same super-hot mineral water already used to generate electricity, companies can bypass the massive ecological destruction of traditional open-pit mining and sprawling evaporation ponds. While this double-dipping method sounds like the ultimate eco-friendly victory for the electric vehicle industry, it completely ignores the terrifying environmental reality of California's severe water shortages. As massive industrial water demands threaten to shrink the Salton Sea even faster, rapidly receding shorelines are exposing miles of highly toxic, sediment-heavy lakebeds to the open wind. Click the video to uncover the dark side of America's new Lithium Valley and find out exactly why this so-called green miracle is blasting dangerous, lung-damaging dust directly into local communities.

Trace the ancient origins of toys and games throughout history, and discover how play has evolved — and stayed the same.

In the Indus Valley a thousand years later, a toddler giggled at the sound of their terracotta whistle. So, what other playthings have delighted us through history? Trace the ancient origins of toys, games, and play traditions.
